verdict: READY TO MERGE - 12 of 12 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: table.test.ts exercises the pure table with real buildRow rows at a fixed UTC offset, so expected clock strings hold on any host; no stubs of the code under test.
The wide-terminal test pins every line of the output exactly, including padding, right-alignment colons in the delimiter and the wake/since-prompt cells.
parseLapArgs tests cover order independence, case folding, the default limit and the duplicate/zero/negative/fractional refusals.

lap.test.ts drives /lap-times end to end through the engine with a fake host (command.register recorder, in-memory laps file), including idempotent registration across two session starts and pass-through outside a harness project.
The 'all' test seeds a foreign session row in the laps file and proves the default view filters it while 'all' shows it.
parseRows now delegates to parseAllRows, so the session and all-sessions readers share one lenient line parser instead of a duplicate.
table.ts is pure and its width arithmetic is exact: rowWidth matches both the padded content lines and the delimiter line, and right-aligned delimiters keep the same width.
The command reads rows through serial(), so a /lap-times never interleaves with a stop's read-modify-write of the laps file.
Pipe escaping happens before width measurement, so an escaped cell never misaligns its column.
parseLapArgs rejects duplicates, zero and leading-zero counts, returning the usage line rather than guessing.

README drop order (stop reason, wake, session, #, date, kind, since prompt) matches the dropRank values in plugins/lap-stamp/hooks/table.ts:30-40 exactly, and the always-kept Stop and Lap match dropRank 0.
README example table's padding, right-aligned delimiter rows (`--:`, `-------:`) and column widths reproduce what `tableLines` emits, so the sample is a faithful rendering rather than hand-drawn.
The claim that output stays out of model requests is grounded: the handler returns `isTextDisplayOnly: true`, whose host contract says the row goes in no request.
TASK-10 receipt provenance checks out: tree 4f6cd3a is the tree of commit 8d1c2dd, and the shape matches the earlier sealed receipts.
EX6 records the design reason a mod command was chosen over a skill (only command.run carries presentation.columns), which is the non-obvious constraint a later reader needs.
table.ts is pure, and its tests pin exact line-by-line output for the wide, narrow, all-sessions, limited and empty cases, so a regression in the table shape cannot slip past.
parseRows now delegates to the new parseAllRows instead of duplicating the line loop, so the BOM and malformed-line handling lives in one place.

The README drop order (stop reason, wake, session, #, date, kind, since prompt) matches the dropRank values in table.ts exactly, and the README example table is the exact output asserted in table.test.ts.

The command answers with isTextDisplayOnly and passes command.run through when unregistered; a lap.test.ts case covers the non-project pass-through, so the mod stays inert outside harness projects as the root README claims.
DesignEvolution EX6 records the scope addition against TASK-7, including why a mod command was chosen over a skill: only command.run carries presentation.columns.
parseRows now delegates to parseAllRows, so the single-session and all-session parsers cannot drift apart.
Column fitting keeps Stop and Lap pinned (dropRank 0) and the loop breaks when nothing droppable remains, so a tiny width never loops forever.
rowWidth matches the rendered line and delimiter widths exactly (1 + sum(w + 3)), including right-aligned `-:` delimiters.
Stop and Date both read the stored ISO text as written, so date and clock stay consistent across offsets and DST.
The command answers with isTextDisplayOnly and passes through to `next` when unregistered, covered by the pass-through test outside a harness project.
parseLapArgs rejects 0, negatives, decimals and duplicate tokens, with tests for each.

important.name: /lap-times failure branches untested
important.summary: lap.test.ts's module doc (lines 11-12) claims coverage of 'every way a host call can fail', and the new /lap-times glue adds three failure paths: a refused command.register leaves the command unregistered so command.run passes through (lap.ts:337-346, 370), an unreadable laps file under 'all' answers LAP_TIMES_UNAVAILABLE (lap.ts:354-356, 364), and a throw inside the handler answers LAP_TIMES_UNAVAILABLE only while registered (lap.ts:373-375). The new describe block (lap.test.ts:778-830) covers only the happy paths, the usage line and the no-harness.json pass-through; none of these branches has a test, so a regression in them (e.g. setting isCommandRegistered before the register promise resolves) goes unseen.
fix: Add tests in the '/lap-times' block: (1) on('command.register', () => ({ deny: 'no' })) then start, expect seen.commands empty and a downstream on('command.run', () => ({ text: 'beneath' })) to answer; (2) seen.unreadable.add(LAPS) after a turn, expect lapTimes($, 'all') text toBe 'lap-stamp: the laps file could not be read.'

important.name: /lap-times 'this session' shows the last known session, not the current one
important.summary:
lapTimesRows (lap.ts:349-353) is documented as returning 'the current session's [rows] from memory', but it reads sessionAtom, which holds the last session the glue loaded or stopped in. The clockFor docstring (lap.ts:94-99) states that a /clear or a resume raises no session.start, so after a /clear (or a resume not followed by session.attach) and before the first stop in the new session, `/lap-times` prints the previous session's rows under the summary label 'this session' (table.ts:93), and a resumed session's earlier rows in the laps file are not shown at all.

Also (runtime): registerLapTimes (lap.ts:337-346) is documented 'once per load' but registers once per ctx lifetime: after the first success, isCommandRegistered stays true forever. A later session.start that resolves to no project (watchOf returns undefined) leaves the command live; `/lap-times all` then answers 'the laps file could not be read' (lap.ts:354-356) instead of passing on, and if the host drops command registrations on a new session the flag prevents re-registering. pytest-scope registers on every session.start without a flag (scope.ts:631-636).

Also (roast): The default view reads rowsAtom (lap.ts:352), which load() builds with mergeRows (lap.ts:322), so it includes held rows whose file write was refused. The `all` view parses only the laps file (lap.ts:354-356). A turn whose write failed is therefore counted by `/lap-times` and missing from `/lap-times all`, so the two summaries disagree on this session's turn count and total. It is an edge case, but the command exists to report those totals.
fix: In lapTimesRows, read the live id with sessionIdOf($); when it differs from sessionAtom (or sessionAtom is null), read the laps file and return parseRows(text, live) (undefined when the file does not read), otherwise keep the in-memory rows.
Alternatively return [] when the live session id differs from sessionAtom, so the table never labels another session's rows as 'this session'.

Register on every load in an active project (drop the early return, as pytest-scope does) and gate the command.run handler on the current watch (ctx.watch !== undefined) rather than on a flag set once.
Or at minimum reword the registerLapTimes docstring to 'once per registration' and reset isCommandRegistered when load resolves to no project.

In lapTimesRows' all branch, merge the in-memory rows the file lacks: `mergeRows(parseAllRows(text), await read($, rowsAtom))`, and add a lap.test.ts case with an unwritable laps file that expects the held row under `all`.
Or document in the README's /lap-times section that `all` shows only rows that reached the file.

minor.name: Release note folds #351's /lap-times into the #349 entry
minor.summary: docs/RELEASES/v1.1.0.md appends the `/lap-times [all] [N]` sentence to the `#349 Feat(lap-stamp): new mod` entry, so the release notes attribute this PR's command to #349. The project's release convention is one line per change; lap-stamp is unreleased (0.1.0, v1.1.0 not cut), so folding is defensible, but the PR number is then lost from the notes.
fix: Add a separate `- #351 Feat(lap-stamp): /lap-times ...` line after the #349 entry and keep the #349 entry to the mod itself.
Keep the fold and add `(#351)` after the `/lap-times` sentence.

minor.name: /lap-times registration described as session.start only
minor.summary: The hooks table says `/lap-times` is registered at `session.start`, and EX6's new_outcome says the same. In code `registerLapTimes` runs from `load` (plugins/lap-stamp/hooks/lap.ts:313-315), which both the `session.start` and `session.attach` hooks call (lap.ts:436-446), so the command is registered at the first load of either event in an active project. The session.start/session.attach row of the table also says only that it loads rows.
fix: README line 126: say `/lap-times` is registered at the first `session.start` or `session.attach` in an active project; EX6 new_outcome (DesignEvolution.json:166): `at session.start or session.attach`.

minor.name: /lap-times example shows an impossible wake lap
minor.summary:
The README example has a prompt turn stopping at 14:00:05 with lap 5s (prompt pressed at 14:00:00), then a wake turn stopping at 14:01:15 with lap 1m 15s and since prompt 1m 15s. Per the Lap rules section a wake lap runs from its own start to its stop, and that start cannot precede the previous turn's stop at 14:00:05, so the lap is at most 1m 10s while since prompt (from 14:00:00) is 1m 15s. Lap equal to since prompt on a wake row contradicts the rules the same README states.

Also (docs): README line 130-131 says the summary line carries 'turn count, total lap, longest lap'. `summaryLine` (table.ts:92-101) also carries the scope (`this session` or `all sessions (<count>)`) and appends `last N shown` when the limit trims rows; `lapTimesText` prints `no turns recorded in ... yet` for zero rows and lap.ts:335 prints `lap-stamp: the laps file could not be read.` when `all` cannot read the file. A reader of the README cannot predict those outputs.
fix: Set the wake row's Lap cell to `1m 10s` (same 6-char width, padding unchanged) and the summary line to `lap total 1m 15s · longest 1m 10s`.

Extend the /lap-times paragraph: the summary names the scope (with the session count under `all`) and adds `last N shown` when rows are trimmed; an empty scope prints a 'no turns recorded' line and an unreadable laps file prints a one-line failure.

minor.name: Width guarantee overclaims for terminals narrower than Stop + Lap
minor.summary:
README states 'No line is wider than the terminal at the moment the command runs' and the table.ts module docstring says 'Every table line fits the terminal width'. `fitColumns` (table.ts:71-80) breaks out of the loop when only dropRank-0 columns (Stop, Lap) remain, so a terminal narrower than those two columns (about 18+ cells, more with `1h 59m` laps) still gets lines wider than the terminal. The code behavior is sensible; the absolute claim is not what it does.

Also (roast): The lap-stamp README (line 145) promises that no line is wider than the terminal, and the table.ts module comment (lines 6-7) says every table line fits the terminal width. fitColumns (table.ts:71-80) stops dropping once only Stop and Lap remain, so any terminal narrower than about 18 columns gets a wider table. table.test.ts:88-91 pins exactly that: at columns 10 the header is '| Stop     | Lap |' (18 characters). The docs make a promise the test proves false.
fix: README line 145-147 and table.ts:6: qualify the claim, e.g. 'columns go least useful first ... until the table fits or only the stop time and the lap remain'.

Qualify the claim in plugins/lap-stamp/README.md:145 and plugins/lap-stamp/hooks/table.ts:6-7: lines fit the terminal down to the width the stop time and lap columns need, and below that the two-column table is printed as is.
Alternatively, in lapTimesText, cut each table line to opts.columns with the same ellipsis summaryLine uses when the kept columns still overflow, and change table.test.ts:88-91 to assert that width.

minor.name: `all` view omits held rows that the session view shows
minor.summary: The session view reads rowsAtom, which keeps rows whose file write was refused (mergeRows, lap.ts:68-72, 319-323); the `all` view reads only parseAllRows(text) (lap.ts:356). A refused-write row appears under `/lap-times` but vanishes under `/lap-times all`, so the two views disagree on the current session's turn count and totals.
fix: In lapTimesRows' all-sessions branch, return mergeRows(parseAllRows(text), await read($, rowsAtom)) so held rows of the current session are included.

minor.name: Module doc overstates the width guarantee
minor.summary: table.test.ts:8 says the table is one 'whose every line fits the terminal width', yet the test at table.test.ts:88-91 pins a header '| Stop     | Lap |' (18 wide) at columns 10, since Stop and Lap are never dropped. The same unqualified claim sits in table.ts:6-7 ('Every table line fits the terminal width'), which the next clause contradicts.
fix: Qualify both docstrings: 'every line fits the terminal width, down to the stop time and lap, which are never dropped'.

minor.name: Module docstring promises every line fits the width; the never-dropped columns can overflow
minor.summary: table.ts:6-7 says 'Every table line fits the terminal width', but fitColumns breaks out of its loop when only rank-0 columns (Stop, Lap) remain (table.ts:75), so a narrow terminal gets lines wider than `columns`; table.test.ts:88-91 pins exactly that ('| Stop     | Lap |' at columns 10). The README makes the same absolute claim (README.md:145).
fix: Reword table.ts:6-7 to 'Every table line fits the terminal width when Stop and Lap alone fit: columns are dropped least useful first, and the stop time and the lap are never dropped, even past the width.' and the README sentence likewise.

minor.name: Spread into Math.max over every row of the laps file
minor.summary:
summaryLine computes `Math.max(...rows.map(r => r.lap_ms))` (table.ts:95) over all rows, which for `all` is every row of the laps file; the glue already reads files past 4 MiB in ranges (lap.ts:207-231), and a spread past the engine's argument limit throws RangeError. The throw is caught by the command's catch and reported as 'the laps file could not be read', a misleading message. filled (table.ts:67) has the same pattern over the shown rows, which an `N` as large as the file also reaches.

Also (roast): summaryLine computes `Math.max(...rows.map(r => r.lap_ms))` (table.ts:95) over every row in the laps file for `/lap-times all`. filled() does the same with `Math.max(header, ...cells)` (table.ts:67) over the shown rows, and `N` has no upper bound. lap.ts explicitly supports laps files larger than the host's 4 MiB read (RANGE_BYTES ranged reads), so the file is expected to grow without limit. A spread over very large arrays throws RangeError (too many arguments). The command's catch turns that into 'the laps file could not be read', a misleading message for a file that read fine.

Also (adv_code): summaryLine computes `longest` as `Math.max(...rows.map(r => r.lap_ms))` over every row passed in, and in `all` mode that is every row of the laps file (parseAllRows, unbounded). Spreading an array of roughly 125k elements into a call throws RangeError (Maximum call stack size exceeded) on V8; the same holds for `filled` when a user passes a large N. lapTimesText runs outside `serial`, so the throw reaches the command.run `.catch`, which answers `lap-stamp: the laps file could not be read.` -- a readable file is reported as unreadable, permanently once the file passes the threshold.

Attack: In a table.test.ts case: `const rows = Array.from({ length: 130000 }, () => rowAt(5)); lapTimesText(rows, { isAllSessions: true, limit: 50, columns: 100 })` throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded from table.ts:95. Spread limit confirmed with `node -e "Math.max(...new Array(125000).fill(1))"` -> Maximum call stack size exceeded (100000 passes). End to end: a laps file of 130k valid rows (about 45 MB) makes `/lap-times all` answer `lap-stamp: the laps file could not be read.` via the catch at plugins/lap-stamp/hooks/lap.ts:373-375; `/lap-times all 130000` on the same file also throws from table.ts:67.
fix: Use a reduce: `rows.reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.lap_ms), 0)` at table.ts:95 and `cells.reduce((m, c) => Math.max(m, c.length), col.header.length)` at table.ts:67.
Replace both spreads with a reduce: `rows.reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.lap_ms), 0)` in summaryLine, and `cells.reduce((m, c) => Math.max(m, c.length), col.header.length)` in filled().

Compute the longest lap with a reduce: `rows.reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.lap_ms), 0)` in plugins/lap-stamp/hooks/table.ts:95, and the column width in `filled` (table.ts:67) with `cells.reduce((m, c) => Math.max(m, c.length), col.header.length)`.

minor.name: Column fitting ignores the columns <= 0 case the summary line guards
minor.summary:
summaryLine treats `opts.columns > 0` as the condition for cutting (table.ts:100), implying a zero width means 'unknown'. fitColumns (table.ts:71-80) has no such guard: with columns 0 every droppable column is removed, so an unknown-width presentation gets only Stop and Lap. The two width rules disagree on what 0 means.

Also (roast): summaryLine (table.ts:100) treats opts.columns <= 0 as an unknown width and does not cut the line. fitColumns (table.ts:73) treats the same 0 as a real width and drops every droppable column, down to Stop and Lap. render.tsx:73 already uses 0 as the 'width unknown' value (`columns ?? 0`), so a host that reports no width would get a full summary over a two-column table. The two helpers in one module disagree on what 0 means.
fix: In fitColumns, return all columns unchanged when columns <= 0 (matching summaryLine), e.g. `if (columns <= 0) return [...all]` before the loop.
Or treat columns <= 0 as a width to fit in both places and drop the `opts.columns > 0` guard in summaryLine.
In fitColumns, return all columns unchanged when columns <= 0 (match the summaryLine guard), and add a table.test.ts case for columns: 0 that expects every column.
Or normalize once in lapTimesText (e.g. a non-positive width becomes Infinity) and drop the special case in summaryLine.

minor.name: Column drop order is never pinned
minor.summary: The test titled 'the least useful columns go first' (table.test.ts:72-81) asserts only that 'Stop reason' and 'Wake' are gone and that 'Stop' and 'Lap' remain. With two rows at 50 columns the rank order in table.ts:30-39 keeps '#', 'Kind' and 'Since prompt' (width 49), but a fitColumns that dropped every droppable column, or dropped by the wrong rank (e.g. 'Since prompt' before 'Wake'), still passes: both end without 'Wake'/'Stop reason'. No other test (lap.test.ts:59-65 checks only width; table.test.ts:88-91 checks only the never-dropped pair) pins which columns survive, and the all-sessions ranks for Session (5), # (4) and Date (3) are never exercised under a narrow width.
fix: Replace the 'toContain'/'not.toContain' checks with an exact header: expect(header).toBe('| # | Stop     | Kind   |    Lap | Since prompt |'), and add an all-sessions case at a width that drops Session but keeps Date (assert its exact header).
